definition: A neural processing unit (NPU), also known as an AI accelerator or deep learning processor, is a class of specialized hardware accelerator or computer system designed to accelerate artificial intelligence and machine learning applications, including artificial neural networks and computer vision.
details: NPU can be standalone, a part of a central processing unit (CPU) or a part of a graphics processing unit (GPU).

explainer.lead: An NPU is specialised hardware designed to accelerate AI and machine learning workloads such as neural networks and computer vision. It matters because it speeds up these applications beyond what general-purpose chips do.

tiers.eli5: It's a chip built specifically to do the maths of AI models quickly, rather than a general-purpose brain doing everything.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers target NPUs to speed up inference for neural networks and vision tasks, and must account for where the unit sits in the system. A pitfall is that an NPU can be standalone or embedded in a CPU or GPU, which changes integration and performance characteristics.
tiers.paperLevel: An NPU, also called an AI accelerator or deep learning processor, is a class of specialised hardware accelerator or computer system designed to accelerate AI and machine learning applications; it can be standalone or part of a CPU or GPU.

explainer.example: A vision model runs on an NPU embedded in a system-on-chip, executing its neural network operations faster than on the general-purpose processor alone.
